handbook.a11_f: The one thing that matters most about the next match: win and you go top, the board meets on Monday whatever happens, a woman is one try short of fifty, a side you have lost to three times running. It reads the table, the board, the grudges and the milestones and picks the biggest. When there is nothing worth saying, it says nothing.
handbook.a12_f: A great deal. Each referee has his own tolerance, and some will reach for a card where others talk. A yellow puts you a woman down for ten minutes and the scoreboard usually shows it. A red is worse: the player leaves the field, and she picks up a ban of one or more matches afterwards. Aggressive players and the Hot Head trait get carded more.
handbook.a19_f: Because players are people. Every woman has two things the game never shows as a number: how consistent she is week to week, and what a big occasion does to her. Some turn up every Saturday. Some are capable of anything, good or bad. Some grow an inch walking out for a final or a derby, and some freeze. Favourites feel it too: on the big day the gap between the sides closes a little, which is why cup upsets happen. You learn who is who the way a real coach does, by watching a season of ratings. During a match your assistant reports condition the same way, "blowing", "tiring", "out on her feet", because nobody on a touchline knows a woman is at exactly 43%.
handbook.a20_f: What you say to a replacement as she pulls her shirt on, set for each bench seat on the Tactics bench page. Do the same job is neutral. Make an impact buys carrying at the cost of defence, and she tires quickly. Calm it down buys tackling and discipline and takes fewer risks in attack. Kill the clock kicks for territory to keep play in their half. Only the first three briefed replacements to come on take effect, so choose who gets one.
handbook.a21_f: It sets what each player has been told against what the team sheets actually say. Set her role (key player, rotation, squad player, prospect, or not in plans) and the page shows the games she was promised, the games she has had, and how she feels about the gap. A player short of what she was promised gets restless and in the end wants out. An honest role costs you nothing.
handbook.a22_f: Only for leaving out players you told otherwise, and only those outside this week's matchday 23. Nobody in the 23 has a grievance this week. A frozen-out player settles into a grudge rather than sinking further, so it shows up as transfer requests, knocks on your office door and contract trouble, not as a hidden penalty on the side you pick.
handbook.a23_f: Four jobs beyond the armband: who leads the pack, who runs the defensive line, who runs the attack, and who sets the standards. A job does not make the side stronger overall. It moves the leadership you already have onto one area and away from the rest, so a defensive leader sharpens the defence and costs you some attacking shape. Only starters with real authority can take one. A strong leader can take two, but each is its own trade-off: a second job pulls more of the side towards her areas, it does not add a bonus.
handbook.a26_f: Your assistant names the side once and it stays that way: nobody updates a sheet you never touch for form, fitness or new signings. He is decent, not perfect, and misjudges a woman here and there, less often the better his badge. Picking the XV yourself is worth real points over a season, and so is a better assistant if you want to delegate. The press desk is the same: every question you leave unanswered costs a little board confidence and fan mood.
handbook.a27_f: On the Tactics tab each shirt can be given a role that shapes how she plays: a ball-playing ten, a fetcher at seven, a sweeping full-back. A role suits some players more than others, and it works best on a woman whose attributes already point that way.
handbook.a29_f: Pair any player aged 20 or under who is still below her potential with a senior pro of 28 or more, on the Mentoring tab of the Team Report. Four pairings at a time, five with a Centre of Excellence at level 3 or better. Choose the young player first and every senior who could take her is listed with how close their positions are, her leadership, her caps and what she could teach. Nobody knows how the two will get on until they try: for the first month the card only says it is too early to tell, and after that it says in plain words how it is going. Character decides most of it: a Leader teaching an Ambitious or Temperamental kid is the best combination in the game, two Temperamentals together the worst, and a Mercenary teaches almost nothing. The same position helps, the same unit (front row, back five, halves, outside backs) a little, and experience a little more. Each week the pairing can coach a point into something the senior is clearly better at and the kid's position needs, paid for from the kid's least needed attributes like all training, and can add a rating point while she is below her potential: about one a season for an average pairing. A senior can take two kids, but each then learns at three-quarter speed, and she will mention it in the eight-week reports. Slowly the kid may also take on her mentor's character, roughly a one in three chance across a season. The Mentoring tab keeps a record of what each kid has gained. A pairing ends itself when there is nothing left to teach (the kid turns 21, reaches her ceiling or takes on her mentor's character), and one that is not working can be ended on its card.
handbook.a3_f: Yes, at any stoppage. The clipboard button opens tactics and replacements mid-match, so you can shut a game down, chase one, or get a tiring front row off. Eight women sit on the bench and you can use all eight, as the laws allow, front-row cover included. A woman who has come off does not come back, except for blood and front-row cover. The game suggests natural cover first rather than putting a winger in the second row.
handbook.a30_f: Three layers. The whole squad has a weekly emphasis; up to five youngsters can have a development focus for faster growth; and a handful of women can go on personal plans, individual programmes in a chosen area. Your assistant's badge sets how many plans can run at once, the matching specialist coach and the Training Paddock make a plan land more often, and younger women take more from it. A woman on a plan does her programme instead of the squad session, not both. Progress is slow. Training decides where ability goes, not how much there is: every point a programme adds is paid for by a point from an area it does not cover, taken from what the position needs least, and it stops near the level the position plays at. A plan also adds one rating point each summer to anyone below their potential.
handbook.a39_f: A youth intake arrives every season. Your academy coach and the Centre of Excellence both raise the quality of what comes through, and the better your setup the more likely a genuine prospect appears. You get an honest preview before intake day and a graded report afterwards. Development deals run out at 21: promote a girl to a professional contract from her player page before the summer she turns 21, or she leaves as a free agent. You are warned a full season ahead.
handbook.a40_f: Yes, but only when something weakens its hand, and the player page tells you what that is before you bid. The strongest card you can hold is a contract running out in the summer, because they would otherwise lose her for nothing. After that: a woman who has barely played, one who is unhappy, a club sitting in the red, a squad already well stocked in her position, or a player the wrong side of 33. Those stack, up to about a third off in the worst case for the seller. A wanted woman who is playing every week at a solvent club will not move a penny, and the screen says so rather than letting you waste a window finding out.
handbook.a47_f: A player who is performing above her contract will have her camp come knocking. You can meet the demand, haggle a figure of your own, or refuse. Refusing a star has consequences, and so does paying every time.
handbook.a49_f: Yes. On her profile, The Office card lets you praise her form or have a quiet word: two conversations a week across the squad, one per woman. Her personality decides how it lands: a professional answers a warning with work, a mercenary shrugs, and praising a struggling hothead reads as sarcasm. Warning a woman who is playing well insults her, and the dressing room hears about it.
handbook.a5_f: Yes, and Physicality is the dial he decides. Pushing it up buys breakdown power and costs you yellow cards and kickable penalties, and the penalty price scales with the referee in the middle. Measured over eight seasons: in front of a referee who lets a lot go at the tackle, going physical is worth about two and a half points a match to you; in front of one who is fussy there, it costs you about a point and a half. Getting that read right is worth roughly four points a match, which is more than any other single slider is worth on its own. The referee and his interpretations are named on the pre-match briefing before you pick, so the information is always there. Left in the middle the dial costs and buys nothing.
handbook.a71_f: Yes, if one asks. The unions watch managers with a reputation of 64 or better and can call twice a season, the smaller nations first; the biggest only come for names in the mid-80s. Accept from your Manager Profile and you run the country alongside the club. The Club & Country screen has everything: the ranking, the union's confidence, your Test record and the squad for the window. When camp is open you can drop a name and call up the next woman: any qualified player in the game, any age, any rating, only the injured refused. The union sets a maximum squad size and will not let it drop below 23. On a Test weekend your assistant takes any club match while you take the country. Leave the job and your Test record stays on your Manager Profile. You can step down from either job on the same screen. A World Championship is the biggest thing in the game. The Job Centre shows how close your reputation is.
handbook.a83_f: The same contest as a ruck, but the ball carrier is still on her feet and players bind on to her. A strong pack drives it forward, which is how a lot of tries are scored from close range.
handbook.a97_f: The front row is two props and a hooker, the women who meet first in a scrum. Add the two locks and it is the tight five, the pushing engine. The back row, two flankers and a number 8, are the forwards who cover the most ground.
handbook.a98_f: The scrum-half feeds the ball out of every ruck and scrum, so she touches it more than anyone on the pitch. The fly-half decides what happens next: pass, kick or run. Usually the goal kicker too.
handbook.a99_f: The two wings and the full-back: the last line of defence and usually the quickest women in the side. They field kicks, chase them, and finish most of the tries.
handbook.a102_f: A yellow card sends a player to the sin bin for ten minutes and you play a woman short. A red card removes her for the rest of the match. Both cost far more than the penalty that caused them.
handbook.a103_f: A Head Injury Assessment. A player who takes a blow to the head leaves the field to be checked; she returns only if she passes, and the game will not let her back if she does not.

coachfix.attHeadNone: {poss}% of the ball and no tries.
coachfix.attHeadOne: {poss}% of the ball and one try.
coachfix.attHowNarrow: Style is at {n}, which keeps it in the pack. Push it past sixty and the backs will see it.
coachfix.attHowWide: Give the 10 the playmaker role on the Roles tab and drill a different attacking call. We had the ball and never used the width.
coachfix.benchHow: Tap Match-Day Squad at the hour. All {cap} changes are free. Fresh legs for whoever is running on empty: that is what wins tight games.
coachfix.discHowHigh: Physicality is at {n}. Pull it under fifty and the same pack concedes fewer.
coachfix.discHowLow: Drop Physicality a notch and put a leader on culture in the leadership group. Cards are a habit, not luck.
coachfix.discRed: A red card, and down to fourteen for the rest of it.
coachfix.discRedWho: {player} sent off, and down to fourteen for the rest of it.
coachfix.discYcWho: {player} binned: ten minutes a player short.
coachfix.gradeAllDone: Both jobs from last time are done: {fixed}. Good. They listened.
coachfix.gradeBoth: Last time we asked for two things. {fixed} is sorted. {missed} is not.
coachfix.gradeBothMissed: {missed} were the jobs last time, and neither has moved.
coachfix.gradeOneDone: {fixed} is sorted since last time. Keep doing whatever that was.
coachfix.gradeOneMissed: We asked about {missed} last time, and here it is again.
coachfix.howBreakdown: A jackal flanker on Selection, or push Physicality up. Contested ball is won by bodies arriving, not by shape.
coachfix.howBreakdownSel: A jackal flanker on Selection. Contested ball is won by bodies arriving, not by shape, and Physicality is already costing us penalties.
coachfix.howLineout: Get a second genuine jumper into the back five on Selection, and change the lineout call on Set Piece so they stop reading it.
coachfix.howScrum: Pick a heavier front row on Selection, or give a prop the scrummager role on the Roles tab. A dial cannot lift a light tight five.
coachfix.kickOrderHow: Set your first and second kicker on Set Piece. The automatic pick hands the tee to a different player every week.
coachfix.lateHead: They scored {n} of their points after the hour.
coachfix.lateHowFew: You made {changes}. Tap Match-Day Squad at the hour: eight fresh bodies is a weapon you have already paid for.
coachfix.lateHowMany: Drop Tempo so the pack is not running on fumes at sixty, and brief two finishers on the Bench page.
coachfix.lostHead: Lost, and no one number explains it.
coachfix.lostHow: Run one preset for a fortnight rather than a new plan every Saturday. Sides that know their own game win the tight ones.
coachfix.rolesHeadNone: Not one shirt has a role set.

rolesHeadSome.one: Only {n} shirt has a role set.
rolesHeadSome.other: Only {n} shirts have a role set.

coachfix.rolesHow: Tap a shirt on the Roles tab. A scrummager, a jackal, a playmaker: small edges, and we are not taking them.
coachfix.splitHead: The bench split is on automatic.
coachfix.splitHow: Choose 5-3, 6-2 or 4-4 on the Bench page. Six forwards wins a scrum war, four and four covers an injury anywhere.
coachfix.tankHead: Even after {subs} changes we finished on {mine}% to their {theirs}%.
coachfix.tankHow: Lower Tempo, or set the week to fitness on Prep. This is a conditioning problem rather than a tactical one, and the gym level on Club Infrastructure is the long answer.
coachfix.teeHeadOne: A conversion missed off the tee.
coachfix.teeHow: Name your kicking order on Set Piece rather than leaving it to whoever has the best boot on the pitch. A slump is only yours to answer if you chose the kicker.
coachfix.terrHead: We only had {poss}% of the ball.
coachfix.terrHowElse: Lower Tempo so phases last, and set the exit to counter on Set Piece rather than kicking it to their full-back.
coachfix.terrHowKick: Kicking is at {n}, so we hand it back on purpose. Bring it down and keep the ball in hand.
coachfix.terrHowTrade: Kicking at {n} got us out of our 22 and gave them the ball. Keep it there and lower Tempo so our own phases last.
coachfix.wonHead: Nothing broke. Now we do it again.
coachfix.wonHow: Leave the Tactics dials alone and pick the same Selection again. The strongest unit was the {unit} - build next week around it.

venue.cold: Cold, and colder than this lot are used to. Kick it to them and make them handle it.
venue.heat: Heat and humidity nobody in this squad trains in. Hydration and tempo control, or it gets away from us late on.
venue.longHaul: {km}km and {tz} hours of clock change. Long-haul rugby: the squad will not be fresh, whatever the medical room says.
venue.road: {km}km on the road. Not far enough to blame, far enough to notice.

venue.trekTz: A genuine trek at {km}km and {tz} hours of time difference. Travel legs are a factor here.

supporter.refused: The store would not open a purchase for this item. Nothing was charged. Usually this means the product is not active yet, or this account is not on the licence-testing list.
supporter.notOffered: The store is not offering this item to your account at the moment, so nothing was charged. That is a set-up issue on our side, not a problem with your account or device. It may not be on sale in your region yet.
supporter.disabled: Purchases are switched off on this device, so the store would not open. Nothing was charged. Check the purchase restrictions (Screen Time, parental or family controls) in your device settings.
supporter.playBilling: Google Play would not take a payment on this account. Nothing was charged. Play gives this answer when in-app purchases are not supported in the account's country, when the Play Store app needs updating, or when the payment method was declined.
supporter.setup: The store would not open a purchase for this item because of a set-up fault on our side, not yours. Nothing was charged. Try again after the next update.
supporter.notNow: The store would not sell this item just now. Nothing was charged. Check you are online and signed in to the store, then try again later.
supporter.error: Couldn't reach the store. Nothing was charged. Try again later.
supporter.nothingToRestore: Nothing to restore on this account.
supporter.pending: The store is still processing it. You don't need to do anything: it arrives on its own, and Restore picks it up if you close the game first.
supporter.unavailable: There is no store attached to this build, so there is nothing to buy. Nothing is missing from the game.

about.contactBody: A bug, a wrong rating, a name you'd rather wasn't in here: it all reaches the same person, and the Report a Bug screen attaches the details needed to fix it.
about.communityBody: Report problems in any language, share ideas and talk rugby with other managers on the PHASE Discord.
about.privacyBody: The game collects nothing about you and sends nothing anywhere. Careers are saved on this device only, which is why the Save / Load screen has an Export button: it is the only backup there is.
about.sub: what this is, and what it takes: nothing
about.thanks: Built for the love of the game. Thank you for playing it.
about.title: About & legal
about.unofficialBody: PHASE: Rugby Manager is not affiliated with, endorsed by or licensed by any player, club, league or governing body. Club names are real; competitions, grounds and sponsors are renamed or invented. Player names are real, used to identify people in a sporting database and for nothing else. No official badges, kits or logos are included.
about.newsPartnerBody: Ruck ({site}). News from around the league, the rumour mill and the law talk carry the {site} byline and logo.
about.storeBody: Optional extras. None of it plays the matches for you.
about.bridgeBody: The store and the adverts come from the app around the game, not from the game itself. If either says not connected, this build of the app was assembled without that piece and nothing in here can switch it on.
about.bridgeProducts: Products priced by the store: {live} of {asked}

news.dealOff: The window is open, but the deal for {name} has fallen through. {why}
news.koHatTrick: {player} scored a hat-trick for {team} in the {comp} {stage_k}. Knockout rugby does not hand out many of those.
news.koFastestSubj: Fastest knockout try on record: {player}, {min} minutes
news.koFastest: {player} scored for {team} after {min} minutes of the {comp} {stage_k}, the fastest knockout try on record. The old mark was {old}'s, after {oldMin} minutes.
news.dealDone: The window is open and the agreed deal has gone through. {why}
news.startVoid: {player} was not available for selection, so the promised start no longer stands.
news.startBroke: You promised {player} a start in the next match, and it did not happen. A transfer request is on your desk, and it will not be withdrawn.
news.startKept: You said in the press room that {player} would start, and the team sheet agreed. The dressing room noticed.
news.rivalBidLost: {player} has joined {club}, who matched the {fee} fee and offered {wage}/week. What decided it: {why_k}.
news.rivalBidWon: {club} had matched the fee and offered {wage}/week, but {player} chose you. What decided it: {why_k}.
news.rivalBacked: {club} finished behind you, and their board has given {coach} an extra {amount}. They are after a {pos_k}.
news.rivalBackedBoard: {club} finished behind you, and their board has found an extra {amount} to spend. They want a {pos_k}.
news.rivalPushBid: {club} have bid {fee} for {player}, with money their board found after they finished behind you.
news.rivalWhyReturn: a return to a club he knows
news.rivalWhyReturn_f: a return to a club she knows
news.rivalWhyNoTerms: you never put terms to him
news.rivalWhyNoTerms_f: you never put terms to her
news.mentEarly: {kid} and {senior} are still getting to know each other. It will be a few weeks before it shows.
news.mentGrowing: {kid} and {senior} have started to click, and the extras after training are paying a little more each week.

maternity.one: {player} has told the club she is pregnant and will begin maternity leave. Her contract is frozen for the duration and her place in the squad is kept for her return. The medical team expect roughly {n} week before she is back in full training.
maternity.other: {player} has told the club she is pregnant and will begin maternity leave. Her contract is frozen for the duration and her place in the squad is kept for her return. The medical team expect roughly {n} weeks before she is back in full training.

news.fanHeadBig: The terraces are not convinced yet
news.fanHeadSmall: The {short} support are ready to get behind you
news.fanOpenBig: A crowd used to winning has been handed a manager nobody has heard of, and the supporters' forums have noticed.
news.fanOpenMid: The reaction around {city} is wait-and-see. Nobody is thrilled, nobody is furious.
news.fanOpenSmall: There is genuine relief around {city} that somebody has taken the job, and a fair amount of goodwill going with it.
news.fanSceptic1: Never heard of him. Hope the board know something we don't.
news.fanSceptic2: Unproven, at a club this size? That's a gamble with our season.
news.fanSceptic3: I'll judge him in May, not August.
news.fanHopeful1: Fresh ideas, finally. Anything is better than what we had.
news.fanHopeful2: Give him two seasons and a bit of money and see what happens.
news.fanHopeful3: He's said the right things. Now let's see him pick a team.
news.fanPatient1: Steady on. New man, new voice, same old fixture list.
news.fanPatient2: The squad is the squad. He can only work with what's in the building.
news.fanPatient3: First home game will tell us plenty about how he wants to play.
news.squadReadSubj: Your assistant's read on the squad
news.ageOld: experienced, near the end of a cycle
news.watchList:
The scouts' pre-season notes on academy talent.
{list_ll}
news.facDeclined: The board looked at your request for a level {lvl} {name_k} and said no: {why_k}. You can ask again in a couple of months, or sooner if results and the books improve.
news.facNoResults: results have not earned a project like this
news.facNoShare: the club cannot find its share
news.facNoReserves: the reserves are too thin for a project this size
news.facApproved: {cost} has been signed off for a level {lvl} {name_k}, all of it from club funds. The builders move in on Monday and it is about a {weeks}-week build. {desc_k}
news.facApprovedShared: {cost} has been signed off for a level {lvl} {name_k}. The board cover {board} of it and the club pays the other {club}. The builders move in on Monday and it is about a {weeks}-week build. {desc_k}
news.expDeclined: The board has said no to {seats} more seats: {why_k}. Show them a full ground week after week and they will look again.
news.expNoEarly: there is not enough of a season to judge the demand yet
news.expNoEmpty: the ground is only {pct}% full as it is
news.expNoReserves: the reserves will not carry a build this size
news.expNoResults: the board wants better results before it pours concrete
news.expApproved: The board has signed off {cost} for a {seats}-seat stand at {stadium}. The hoardings go up this week and it is a {weeks}-week build. Capacity stays as it is until then, and nothing else gets built in the meantime.
news.drawFinal: It's {opp} in the {comp} final, at {venue} in {city}. {seats} seats, and both sets of supporters will be on the road to fill them.
news.drawHome: The draw is made. {opp} come to you in the {comp} {stg_k}. {tail_k}
news.drawAway: You are on the road: {opp} away in the {comp} {stg_k}. {tail_k}
news.drawTailHome: A home tie, the draw everyone wanted.
news.drawTailAway: A tough place to go, and there is no second leg.
news.finalsWeekend: {venue} hosts both European finals this season: the Continental Shield on the Friday night, the Continental Cup on the Saturday. {seats} seats in {city}. Eight quarter-finalists are left in each, and every one of them has the date circled.
news.finalsWeekend_f: {venue} hosts the Hemispheric Championship final this season. {seats} seats in {city}. Eight quarter-finalists are left, and every one of them has the date circled.
news.natFilled: The squad was short with kick-off coming, so your assistant added {n} to make up the numbers. They were picked on merit, not by you.
news.natName: The camp is open and the sheet is blank. {nationCap_k} need a squad of at least {n} named before the first Test. Everyone available is on the country desk, with the coaches' picks at the top.
news.lionsCallA:
{names} {is_k} going on {tour}. Every player in these islands grows up wanting that call.
{he_k} will be away for the tour window.
news.lionsCallB:
The {tour} squad is out, and the club's name is on it: {names}. Training stopped for the announcement. Nobody minded.
{he_k} will be away for the tour window.
news.callUps: The following players have been called up and will be unavailable during the international window: {names}.
news.lionsHome: Back in club colours after {tour}: {names}. A tour changes a player, and {come_k} back with more to say in this dressing room. The medics are urging care after a long summer.
news.lionsHomeWonSubj: The tourists come home as series winners
news.lionsHomeWon: Home from {tour} with a series win in the luggage: {names}. Expect {him_k} to carry that around the training ground. The medics are still urging care after a long summer.
news.intlBack: Back in club colours: {names}. A Test window takes it out of you, and none of them are fresh this week.
news.mentorLost: With {mentor} gone, {kid} is training alone again. The academy coach will keep an eye on him, but it isn't the same.

wantsTerms.one: {player}'s agent has been on the phone. His client is playing out of his skin (avg {avg}) on {wage}/week, and the market pays well north of that. He has {n} year left, but the agent says his head will drop if this drags on, and other clubs will hear about it.
wantsTerms.other: {player}'s agent has been on the phone. His client is playing out of his skin (avg {avg}) on {wage}/week, and the market pays well north of that. He has {n} years left, but the agent says his head will drop if this drags on, and other clubs will hear about it.

news.agentPublic: Two months without a word from the club, so the agent has gone to the papers: "{player} is one of the best-performing players in the league and the club knows our position." Rival clubs read the papers too.
news.becomesMentor: The coaches have seen it in the little things: the extras after training, the way he talks in the huddle. {player} is starting to carry himself like {mentor}.
news.mentorStart: The old pro and the academy kid: {mentor} will mentor {player} this season. Extras after training, lifts to the ground, the lot.
news.aheadOfSchedule: Good news from the physios: {player} ({injury_k}) is ahead of his rehab targets and available again this week, earlier than expected.
news.backInTrainingV3: Back with the main group this week: {men_l}.
news.wPeaceBrokered: The manager got them in a room and shut the door. Both men came out and trained. Nobody is pretending they are friends, but the squad can get on with its week.
news.wTalksFail: The manager tried to settle it between {a} and {b} and got nowhere. Worse, the squad knows the meeting happened, and that it did not work.
news.wPeace1: Clear-the-air talks at the training ground this week. {a} and {b} trained together on Thursday and the squad say the atmosphere has lifted. One senior player: "It's done. We move."
news.wPeace2: Whatever was said between {a} and {b}, it worked. The pair ran the same drills all week and sat together at lunch.
news.wPeace3: {a} and {b} shook hands in front of the group on Monday and went back to work. There was no statement.
news.wFrosty1: Sources close to the squad say {a} and {b} are still not speaking. Team-mates have started picking sides.
news.wFrosty2: {a} and {b} warmed up at opposite ends of the pitch again this week. The coaches pretend not to notice. The players notice everything.
news.wFrosty3: No thaw yet between {a} and {b}: separate gym slots, separate tables, one very tired captain shuttling between them.
news.wRift: {a} and {b} are understood to have had {flash_k}. Coaches pulled them apart, and neither has been in a good mood since.
news.wCommunity1: The whole squad spent Wednesday coaching at local schools and visiting the children's ward. Corny? Maybe. But the group came back closer, and the supporters noticed.
news.wCommunity2: School visits, hospital wards, a hundred wonky selfies: the squad gave the community its Wednesday. The bus home was loud in the good way.
news.wBoot1: {player} has signed a personal sponsorship with a boot manufacturer. His locker now contains fourteen boxes of boots and one very smug grin.
news.wBoot2: A boot brand has put {player} on a personal deal. The first shipment arrived in club colours; the second, mysteriously, in gold. The forwards have thoughts.
news.wGround1: The head groundsman has banned the forwards from 'his' pitch until Thursday after last week's scrummaging session left it looking ploughed. The pack are training on the back field, muttering.
news.wGround2: An uneasy truce at {stadium}: the groundsman has chalked a line beyond which "no scrummaging shall occur". The pack are testing its legal force one metre at a time.
news.wAdvert1: {player} spent his day off filming an advert for a regional car dealership. Team-mates have already got hold of the script. Expect dramatic readings in the team room.
news.wAdvert2: {player} is the new face of a local bathroom showroom. The billboard goes up next month. The dressing room has already ordered a framed print for his locker.
news.wChef1: The performance department has brought in {chef_k} for the rest of the season. The senior pros are sceptical. The young lads are all-in. Someone has already broken the new equipment.
news.wChef2: {short} have added {chef_k} to the backroom staff. Week one verdict from the front row: "interesting". Week one verdict from the academy: total religious conversion.
news.wBug1: The medical room is standing-room only: {names} have all been laid low by a virus doing the rounds. They'll play if picked, but the tanks won't be full this week. The kit staff are bleaching everything.
news.wBug2: {names} all called in pale and shivering this week. The doctor's diagnosis: "the thing that's going round." They can play, but do not expect eighty full-blooded minutes.
news.wBug3: A virus has gone through the squad and {names} are all below par. Training moved outdoors, soup was served, and the physio room smells of eucalyptus.
news.wTakeoverHardens: The consortium linked with {club} has reportedly entered exclusivity. Due diligence is under way, and the current owners are said to be "open to the right offer". The forums are already spending the money.
news.wTakeoverOff: The money men have walked away from {club}, citing what sources call a "valuation gap". The club statement thanks supporters for their patience and insists it remains "well capitalised". Nobody is convinced.
news.wTakeoverCircle: A wealthy consortium has been linked with a takeover of {club}, though the names change depending on who you ask. A private jet at the local airfield has done a lot of heavy lifting on the fan forums. Most of these stories die quietly.
news.wRumour1: {buyerName} have had scouts at {ownerPoss} last three matches. The man they're watching is {player}.
news.wRumour2: Agents claim {buyer} are readying a {fee} bid for {player}. {owner} insist he is going nowhere.
news.wRumour3: {player} to {buyer}? A source at the player's management agency says "there is interest, and it's serious."
news.wRumour4: Whispers from {buyerCity}: {buyerPoss} head coach has made {player} their number one target.
news.wAgent1: {player} is out of contract at the end of the season and the agent is doing the media rounds: "My client loves the club, but wants to feel loved back. We are listening to what's out there."
news.wAgent2: Six months left on {player}'s deal, and his agent has started picking up on the first ring.
news.wAgent3: The contract clock is ticking on {player}, and this week his agent was photographed at lunch with two directors of rugby who were not yours. Draw your own conclusions. Everyone else has.
news.grForumExitSubj: FAN FORUM: "{starLast} to leave?" thread hits 400 replies in a night
news.grForumExit: One unsourced post claiming {star} has "told friends he wants out" has produced four hundred replies, two spin-off threads and a poll. There is no agent, no journalist and no evidence. Page nine is arguing about the stadium car park. One moderator: "Every year. Same thread. Same fella posting it."
news.grSocialClipSubj: SOCIAL: eleven seconds of {star} in training breaks containment
news.grSocialClip: Two million views and counting for a clip of {star} doing something that should not be physically available to a man that size. The comments are split between awe and accusations of a smaller pitch. {shortPoss} media team have posted it, deleted it, and posted it again with worse music.
news.grPodcastKebabSubj: PODCAST: {star}'s cheat meal confession divides the nation
news.grPodcastKebab: Forty minutes of proper lineout detail got no attention at all. One sentence about a Friday kebab has produced eight hundred quote tweets and a statement from a rival takeaway offering him a sponsorship. The {short} nutritionist has requested a right of reply and has been told the slot is full.
news.grPodcastKebab_f: Forty minutes of proper lineout detail got no attention at all. One sentence about a Friday kebab has produced eight hundred quote tweets and a statement from a rival takeaway offering her a sponsorship. The {short} nutritionist has requested a right of reply and has been told the slot is full.
news.grAiGraphicSubj: BROADCAST: graphics package gives {starLast} six fingers and a new name
news.grAiGraphic: The pre-match player card rendered {star} with an extra finger, a surname spelled two different ways in the same graphic, and a career-tries figure that would make him the leading scorer in the sport's history. The broadcaster has apologised. The screenshot is already a profile picture.
news.grStatAccountSubj: STATS ACCOUNT: {short} are top of a table nobody asked for
news.grStatAccount: A popular numbers account has crunched carries into contact per phase in the opposition 22 on grounds above sea level and declared {short} the best team in the league. Fans of {short} have adopted the metric as gospel. Everyone else has pointed out that it also ranks a pub side above the world champions.
news.grPunditGemSubj: PUNDIT COLUMN: "{short} have unearthed a gem"
news.grPunditGem: This week's big read calls {kid}, {kidAge}, "the most natural {kidPos} of his generation" and notes that half the league already knows. {short} supporters have spent the day asking the columnist, mostly politely, to delete it. He has replied to eleven of them individually.
news.grSchoolVisitSubj: WHOLESOME: {kid} shows up to a school assembly and stays two hours
news.grSchoolVisit: A local primary asked the {short} academy whether anyone could hand out a reading prize. {kid} arrived early, stayed two hours and signed everything put in front of him including the lectern and one teacher's laptop lid. The video has more views than the club's last three tries combined.
news.grAgentFlatteredSubj: AGENT TALK: {target} "flattered" by the interest, says everyone
news.grAgentFlattered: {target}'s representatives had every chance to hose this down and didn't: "My client is very happy at {other}. But every player listens." The fan forums did the rest before lunch.
news.grForumDreamSubj: FAN FORUM: the "realistic transfer targets" thread is anything but
news.grForumDream: The {short} thread is titled "realistic targets" and {target} appears on every page of it. The finances are impossible, the positional fit is questionable and the enthusiasm is absolute. Somebody has made a graphic. Somebody else has made a better one.
news.grRefMicSubj: REF MIC: the clip every group chat is quoting
news.grRefMic: A referee's exchange with a front row from the weekend is in every group chat going: "You are not bound. You have never been bound." Refereeing socials are calling it a masterclass in communication. Props are calling it slander and have opened a group chat of their own.
news.grPropGymSubj: SOCIAL: {propLast} lifts something he should not have lifted
news.grPropGym: {prop} has posted a gym clip that the strength coach describes, on the record, as "not a programmed movement". It has a hundred thousand views and a duet from a professional strongman who appears genuinely concerned. The {short} physio has commented on it too. The comment is one full stop.
news.grPropMarathonSubj: CHARITY: {propLast} agrees to a half marathon, hears "half an hour"
news.grPropMarathon: A supporters' club raffle has committed {prop} to thirteen miles for charity. The acceptance was confident and on camera, followed by a question that revealed the word heard was "half an hour". The fundraising total has tripled since the clip went up.
news.grNineMicSubj: REF MIC: {nineLast} spends eighty minutes coaching the referee
news.grNineMic: The audio from the weekend has {nine} offering the official guidance on the offside line, the tackle height, the clock and, at one point, the official's own positioning. The referee's reply has been turned into a ringtone. Nobody involved regrets anything.
news.grKitLeakSubj: SOCIAL: {shortPoss} new shirt leaks a day early, on a bad mannequin
news.grKitLeak: Next season's kit appeared on a reseller feed before the launch, photographed on a mannequin with one arm and a haunted expression. The club is furious. The fans are not interested in the club's feelings and are holding a referendum on the collar.
news.grGroundsmanSubj: GROUNDSMAN WATCH: visiting coach calls the {stadium} pitch "a ploughed field"
news.grGroundsman: The head groundsman has responded through visibly gritted teeth that "the surface rewards a team willing to keep the ball in hand". The visiting coach has kept a boot as evidence and photographed it next to a ruler. The groundsman has photographed the ruler.
news.grMascotSubj: MASCOT INCIDENT: the {short} mascot is trending for all the wrong reasons
news.grMascot: A half-time penalty shootout ended with the mascot taking out a nine-year-old at the knees and celebrating in front of the family stand. The club has apologised. The mascot has said nothing, stayed in character and gained forty thousand followers overnight.
news.grAnnouncerSubj: STADIUM PA: announcer reads out the wrong team, then doubles down
news.grAnnouncer: The {stadium} announcer named the entire opposition XV as the home side, realised at fifteen, and elected to finish the list anyway "for consistency". The crowd applauded every name. Away supporters have started a petition to have him do their team sheet every week.
news.grPieSubj: CATERING: the {short} pie has been reviewed, and the review is 900 words
news.grPie: A widely followed food account has awarded the ground's steak pie a mark of 6.4 with the note "structurally ambitious, emotionally cold". The club has responded by putting the score on a chalkboard outside the kiosk. Sales are up thirty per cent. The pie has not changed.
news.grDroneSubj: TRAINING LEAK: a drone over {short} training gets exactly nothing
news.grDrone: Somebody flew a drone over a closed session hoping for the team sheet and captured forty minutes of a squad doing a passing drill in complete silence, plus one man tying a lace for nine of them. The footage has been posted anyway. It has done numbers.
news.grSeagullSubj: WILDLIFE: a seagull holds up play at {stadium} for two minutes
news.grSeagull: A single gull occupied the 22 and declined every invitation to leave, including one from a second row who tried reasoning. Play resumed when the bird took a pie from row three and departed on its own terms. It now has a fan account with more followers than two of the players.
news.grMerchTypoSubj: MERCH: {short} sell out of a shirt with a spelling mistake on it
news.grMerchTypo: A print run went out with the club motto missing a letter, which the club discovered from a supporter's post rather than from the supplier. The recall lasted ninety minutes before somebody noticed the mistaken ones were reselling for triple. The recall has been quietly cancelled.
news.grBannerSubj: TERRACES: {short} fans unveil a banner nobody can read
news.grBanner: Months of planning went into a full-length tifo for the weekend, and it went up upside down and back to front. From the far stand it appears to say something rude about {short} themselves. The group behind it has declared this "the intended reading all along" and is taking commissions.
news.grStreamSubj: BROADCAST: the {short} stream cuts to a fixed shot of a car park for six minutes
news.grStream: A gallery mix-up sent the live feed to an unmanned camera pointed at the players' entrance during the busiest passage of the match. Nineteen thousand people watched a car park and, by minute four, were commentating on it. The clip has outperformed the highlights.
news.grSponsorSubj: SPONSORS: {shortPoss} new partner is a funeral director and the fans love it
news.grSponsor: The commercial team expected a mild reaction to the sleeve deal and instead got the best day their social accounts have ever had. Supporters were asked for a slogan and thousands answered, most unprintable. The winner goes on the sleeve next week: "With you at the death."
news.grWeatherSubj: WEATHER: hail stops the {short} warm-up and starts a snowball fight
news.grWeather: Sixty seconds of freak hail emptied the pitch and produced footage of two professional squads abandoning their preparation to pelt each other in front of an empty stand. Both head coaches have described it as "not ideal". Both clubs' accounts have posted it.
news.grBusSubj: LOGISTICS: the {short} team bus takes a wrong turn into a wedding
news.grBus: A satnav sent the coach down a lane and into the car park of a hotel mid-reception. The squad were applauded in, photographed with the couple, and applauded out. The bride's cousin has since been photographed at {stadium} in a replica shirt.
news.grQuizSubj: SOCIAL: {short} players fail a quiz about their own club, publicly
news.grQuiz: The media team filmed a light-hearted club history quiz and released it without watching it back. Nobody named the ground's record attendance, one man guessed the club was founded in 1998, and the captain named a competition that has never existed. It is the club's most watched video of the season.
news.grCatSubj: WILDLIFE: a cat is now a member of the {short} coaching staff
news.grCat: A stray that adopted the training ground gates has been photographed sitting in on the forwards' meeting, on the whiteboard side of the room. The club has given it a name, a bowl and, this week, a squad number in the region of 47. The kit man is drafting a shirt.
news.grTmoSubj: TMO: eight minutes to decide something everybody in the ground had decided
news.grTmo: The weekend's showpiece stopped for eight minutes while officials examined a grounding from eleven angles, four of them worse than the naked eye. The eventual decision matched the first replay. Broadcasters have cut it into a montage with a ticking clock and it is doing very well.
news.grKickerNetSubj: SOCIAL: a supporter lands a halfway kick and the internet demands a contract
news.grKickerNet: A half-time competition entrant in jeans and work boots struck one from inside their own half and straight through, then did it again for the cameras. Two clubs have posted the clip. One head coach has been asked about it in a press conference and did not entirely rule it out.
news.grSheepSubj: VILLAGE RUGBY: match abandoned when forty sheep occupy the home 22
news.grFloodlights: The floodlights at {stadium} failed with twenty minutes to play, and the match finished in a gloom with no TMO and no cameras. The scoreboard was not kind to {short}. Supporters have called the power cut the kindest thing to happen to them all season.
news.grHarbourShield: {short} celebrated a cup win with a boat trip round the harbour, and the trophy went over the side before the first drink was poured. A club volunteer who dives at weekends brought it back up ten minutes later. The trophy has been polished. The volunteer has been given a season ticket and the captaincy of the boat.
news.grInflatablesSubj: {short} ban inflatables from the team bus
news.grInflatables: Ahead of the annual fancy dress trip, {short} have banned inflatables from the team bus. The club will not say what happened last year. The driver will, to anyone who asks, and at length.
news.grStormPizza: Storms held up kick-off at {stadium} for nearly three hours. {short} insist the squad stayed focused throughout. The delivery driver who carried eleven large pizzas down the tunnel tells a different story.
news.grLightning: Lightning over {stadium} ended a match in the 68th minute, and the score at the time stands as the result. {short} were a point ahead. Nobody at the club has ever been so grateful for weather.
news.grDeer: A deer ran the full length of the pitch at {stadium} and flattened {star} on the way through. Player and deer are both fine. The deer has not been cited, although the {short} defence coach has asked for its contact details.
news.grGripMachine: {star} broke the grip-strength machine in the fan zone at the first attempt. The sponsor has promised a sturdier model, and an invoice. The broken one is now on display in the {short} clubhouse, with a small brass plaque.
news.grTattooPact: {star} has promised to have the head coach's face tattooed on a calf if {short} win the league. The coach has asked that a flattering photo be used. The club photographer has been put on standby, just in case.
news.grAirportCafe: {star} was still in the airport café, finishing a toastie, when the {short} flight took off. The player arrived four hours later by a connection nobody can pronounce, and has been fined exactly the price of the toastie.
news.grFeedsSix: A steakhouse near {stadium} advertises a platter that "feeds six". {prop} finished it alone and then asked to see the dessert menu. The restaurant has named the platter after the player and quietly put the price up.
news.grBarbecue: At a {short} squad barbecue, {prop} was promoted to head chef inside five minutes and would not give the tongs back for the rest of the evening. Reviews are mixed. One team-mate described the sausages as "structurally sound".
news.grHeatwave: A heatwave has baked the pitch at {stadium} so hard that {short} have called off contact training. The squad played touch rugby in the car park instead, and {prop} spent most of it stretching in the shade of the team bus.
news.grLovelyDecision: The referee's microphone caught {nine} saying "lovely decision, sir" seconds before the next penalty went the other way. The clip has been watched across the league, and the {short} squad have appointed {nineLast} their official diplomat, effective immediately.
news.grGoldenPoint: Ever since golden point was mentioned at a league meeting, {kid} has practised drop goals in the {short} car park every evening. Three car windows have been replaced so far. The club has bought a net.
news.grKitClash: The kit man packed the {short} home strip for the trip to {other}, who wear almost exactly the same colours. {short} played the first half in training bibs. The kit man has been given a laminated calendar and a long look.
news.grPlaylist: The {other} coach walked out of the post-match press conference after four minutes, because the music from the {short} dressing room next door was too loud to hear the questions. {short} have apologised and released the playlist. It has had more listens than the highlights.
news.grWanderingFanSubj: A new voice in the {short} end
news.grWanderingFan: A young {other} supporter wandered into the {short} end at half-time, was adopted by the choir and went home knowing every song. The family report that the singing has not stopped since. The choir has asked about availability for next season.
news.chTale9Subj: CLUBHOUSE: one answer fits all at quiz night
news.chTale9: {prop} has been banned from the team quiz for answering every question with "scrummaging". It was the right answer twice. The quizmaster says that is exactly the problem.
news.chTale10: Someone has been eating the kit man's sandwiches from the fridge. A notice has gone up, the physio has been appointed to investigate, and three props have produced alibis nobody asked for. The sandwiches are now labelled in capital letters.
news.chTale11: {wing} has been doing sprint drills on the beach at dawn. On the first morning a dog joined in. By the third there was a small crowd, a man selling coffee, and a local reporter timing the dog.
news.chTale12: The dressing-room playlist has become a matter of real tension. The forwards want power ballads, the backs want something with a drop in it, and the kit man has been caught adding brass bands. A committee has been formed. It has not met, because nobody can agree on the music.
news.grSheep: A gate left open at a sixth-tier fixture let an entire flock in while a penalty advantage was being played. The referee consulted both captains, consulted the sheep, and abandoned the game with the line: "Gentlemen, they have more numbers and better shape than either defence." The league has ordered a replay. The farmer has ordered a season ticket.
news.grTrophyLostSubj: SILVERWARE: a village club has been polishing the wrong trophy for 42 years
news.grTrophyLost: During an insurance valuation, the county junior cup a village side has displayed since 1984 turned out to be a regional best-kept-allotment award with a rugby ball soldered on. Nobody knows where the real cup went. The club has voted unanimously to keep the allotment one, on the grounds that "we definitely won something, and this is shinier."
news.grPostmanSubj: GRASSROOTS: fourth-tier club discovers their postman has been at every away game for 20 years
news.grPostman: A club historian putting together an anniversary album noticed the same figure at the edge of every away photograph since 2006. It is their postman, who has never once mentioned it on the round. Asked why, he said he didn't want a fuss. The club has retired the number 24 in his honour, which he has described as a fuss.
news.grDogTrySubj: VILLAGE RUGBY: a dog scores the decisive try and the league has to rule on it
news.grDogTry: A spaniel invaded a promotion decider, intercepted a flat pass and crossed the line to what witnesses describe as the loudest cheer in the ground's history. The referee disallowed it for offside, reasoning the dog "entered from in front of the kicker". The league has upheld the decision but named the spaniel in its team of the week, at openside.
news.grAnthemSubj: MATCHDAY: the wrong anthem plays and both teams commit to it completely
news.grAnthem: An admin error at a cup tie played the theme from a daytime antiques programme instead of the national anthem. Neither side broke formation. Thirty professional rugby players stood at full attention through ninety seconds of light harpsichord, hands on hearts, and the crowd joined in humming. The clip has more views than the match.
news.grScrumCafeSubj: COMMUNITY: a front row opens a coffee shop where everything is scrum-named and nothing is explained
news.grScrumCafe: Three retired props have opened a cafe with a menu that includes the Loosehead Latte, the Tighthead Flat White and a pastry called the Collapsed Maul, which arrives deliberately flattened. Tourists keep asking why the sugar sachets say "BIND" on them. The owners refuse to say. It is the best-reviewed coffee shop in the county.
news.grLineoutLadderSubj: GRASSROOTS: club banned from using their new lineout tactic involving an actual stepladder
news.grLineoutLadder: An eighth-tier side unveiled a routine in which the hooker threw to a jumper standing on a stepladder painted in club colours. It worked three times before the referee found the relevant law, which took eleven minutes, because nobody had ever needed it before. The league's written ruling begins "with reluctant admiration" and the ladder now hangs in the clubhouse.
news.grFogMatchSubj: WEATHER: two teams play twelve minutes in fog before discovering the ball went home
news.grFogMatch: A cup tie in dense fog continued in fine spirit until both packs converged on a ruck that turned out to be a training bag. Investigation revealed a clearing kick in the third minute had left the ground entirely, and a spectator, believing the game over, had taken the ball home for a child. The league has ordered a replay. The child is keeping the ball.
news.chTale1Subj: CLUBHOUSE: {propLast} wins the squad golf day, refuses to be humble
news.chTale1: {prop} shot the round of his life at the team golf day and has already had the scorecard laminated. It is now blu-tacked inside his locker at eye level. The backs have demanded a recount; the referee (the kit man) says the result stands.
news.chTale2Subj: CLUBHOUSE: ice bath declared too small for the front row
news.chTale2: The new recovery suite opened this week, and within a day the front row lodged a formal complaint that the ice bath "fits one and a half props maximum". A rota has been posted. {prop} has annexed the 6pm slot indefinitely and laminated that too.
news.chTale3Subj: CLUBHOUSE: {lockLast} adopts the groundsman's dog, sort of
news.chTale3: The groundsman's terrier has decided {lock} is its favourite person on earth and now attends every session, sitting neatly beside the tackle bags. The club shop is printing a tiny replica shirt. Nobody has told the groundsman where his dog spends its days, but he probably knows.
news.chTale4Subj: CLUBHOUSE: half-backs in bus playlist standoff
news.chTale4: {nine} and {ten} have shared control of the team bus playlist for two seasons, and the arrangement has finally collapsed over what the squad describe only as "the incident with the sea shanties". A peace deal now alternates song by song. The forwards, who wanted silence, have lost again.
news.chTale5Subj: CLUBHOUSE: {wingLast} loses race to a schoolboy, demands rematch
news.chTale5: At a community visit this week the fastest man at the club was beaten over 40 metres by a twelve-year-old wearing school shoes. {wing} maintains the start was jumped and has formally requested a rematch "on a proper track, with blocks". The twelve-year-old's PE teacher is considering terms.
news.chTale6Subj: CLUBHOUSE: team-room quiz night ends in googling scandal
news.chTale6: Wednesday's quiz night was abandoned at the sports round when one table of forwards answered a question about 1987 with suspicious speed and in full sentences. Phones are now surrendered at the door, and the quizmaster (the physio) has been given "full disciplinary powers". He has had a lanyard made. Nobody knows how to tell him it has gone too far.
news.chTale7Subj: CLUBHOUSE: the kit man's biannual sock audit strikes fear into all
news.chTale7: It is sock audit week. The kit man has counted out, counted back, and found the squad collectively nine pairs short. An amnesty box has appeared outside the changing room with a sign reading "NO QUESTIONS ASKED (THIS TIME)". Three pairs have already been returned under cover of darkness.
news.chTale8Subj: CLUBHOUSE: bus driver gets a guard of honour for his 200th away trip
news.chTale8: Two hundred away trips, zero breakdowns, one legendary flask. The squad formed a guard of honour in the car park this week for the team bus driver, who described it as "completely unnecessary" while visibly delighted. He has been presented with a shirt with WHEELS 1 on the back.
news.lawWatch1Subj: LAW WATCH: 25-point "super try" floated for length-of-the-field scores
news.lawWatch1: A working group has proposed quintuple points for tries begun behind a team's own 22. Coaches call it "bingo rugby". Fans have already built entire imaginary seasons around it. The world governing body stresses it is "one idea among many", which is committee language for never.
news.lawWatch2Subj: LAW WATCH: proposal to reduce teams to 13 players "under review"
news.lawWatch2: A discussion paper suggests trimming the XV to thirteen to "open space and cut collisions". The northern unions are apoplectic, the southern unions intrigued, and one existing sport with exactly that player count is watching with its arms folded. Expect a quiet burial by autumn.
news.lawWatch3Subj: LAW WATCH: shot clock for scrums - 30 seconds or a free-kick
news.lawWatch3: The proposal: packs get half a minute from mark to engagement or concede the put-in. Front rows everywhere describe the idea as "a war crime". Referees privately love it. The trial is earmarked for a development competition nobody can name.
news.lawWatch4Subj: LAW WATCH: kicks at goal worth less in the final quarter, says think-tank
news.lawWatch4: Penalties would drop to two points after the hour "to encourage ambition". Kickers are furious, flankers delighted, and the fan forums have run the numbers on every classic final and declared history itself invalid. The world governing body thanks the think-tank for its input.
news.lawWatch5Subj: LAW WATCH: unlimited substitutions trial mooted for pre-season
news.lawWatch5: Rolling subs, all match, every match. Conditioning coaches are delighted. Purists are drafting letters with footnotes. The proposal is at "concept stage", and nobody has said which concept.
news.lawWatch6Subj: LAW WATCH: golden point extra time for all league matches "on the table"
news.lawWatch6: No more draws, ever, says the paper: first score after 80 minutes wins it. The romantics mourn the honourable draw and the broadcasters have already cut a trailer. The league's fixture staff, asked to model the extra time, sent back a single spreadsheet cell reading "no".
news.lawTalk1Subj: LAW WATCH: kicks at goal could be put on a shorter clock
news.lawTalk1: A proposal on the table would trim the shot clock for conversions and penalty kicks by another fifteen seconds. Kickers say their routines are already timed to the breath. Supporters with a last train to catch are broadly in favour. Nothing changes this season.
news.lawTalk2Subj: LAW WATCH: captain's challenge proposed for league matches
news.lawTalk2: Each captain would get one review a match to send a try, a card or a knock-on upstairs, and keep it if proved right. Referees are cautiously open to it. Captains are already practising drawing the rectangle in the air. The idea goes to the next law review.
news.lawTalk3Subj: LAW WATCH: lower tackle height trial floated for the elite game
news.lawTalk3: The community game already tackles below the sternum, and a working group wants the same line trialled at the top level. Backers point to fewer head contacts; doubters fear more offloads than anyone can defend. Any trial would start in a development competition.
news.lawTalk4Subj: LAW WATCH: a limit on scrum resets under discussion
news.lawTalk4: The proposal: two resets, then the referee must award a penalty or a free-kick, or play on. Front rows call it the end of an art form. Everyone watching the clock calls it overdue. A long debate is expected, with at least one strongly worded letter from a tighthead.
news.lawTalk5Subj: LAW WATCH: goal-line drop-out could make way for the five-metre scrum
news.lawTalk5: Held up over the line, and the defence currently gets a goal-line drop-out. A group of coaches wants the old attacking scrum five metres out back instead. Defence coaches are quietly hoping the committee says no. The paper goes to the law review panel in the spring.
news.lawTalk6Subj: LAW WATCH: a foul-play bunker could come to the league
news.lawTalk6: The idea: a yellow card for foul play is reviewed off the field during the ten minutes, and upgraded if the bunker sees something worse. Fans worry about more waiting around; officials say the referee simply gets on with the game. Any change would be next season at the earliest.
news.wWin1: Three wins on the spin and the {stadium} bars are humming. A supporters' podcast this week: "Whisper it, but this {manager} side might actually be building something."
news.wWin2: Three straight wins and the queue at the club shop has opinions about silverware. The older heads keep saying "long season" and grinning while they say it.
news.wWin3: The terraces have a new song and it has {manager} in it. Three wins running will do that. There is already talk of a second verse.
news.wWin4: Three on the bounce, and the man who runs the burger van says takings are up. "Winning makes them hungry."
news.wWin5: A lad in the family stand has started bringing a homemade cardboard trophy. Three straight wins. His dad keeps apologising to the row behind and nobody minds.
news.wWinOn1: The winning run rolls on and the ground has stopped whispering about it. Away fans turn up expecting the worst now.
news.wWinOn2: Still winning. The older heads have given up saying "long season" and started asking about final tickets, quietly, in case saying it out loud breaks something.
news.wWinOn3: The run goes on, and the club shop has sold out of scarves in October. Somebody in the sponsors' lounge used the word "era". Nobody laughed.
news.wLose1: Three straight defeats and the phone-ins have turned. One season-ticket holder of 30 years: "I don't see a plan out there."
news.wLose2: Three losses in a row and the fan forum's match thread got locked by midnight. The mood is not mutinous yet, but the mods are stretched thin.
news.wLose3: Three defeats in a row, and the late radio show on the drive home was brutal. Not one caller had a good word to say.
news.wLose4: Third defeat running and the club shop has quietly moved the replica shirts away from the window. Nobody ordered that. Everybody understood it.
news.wLose5: After a third straight loss the fanzine ran a blank page with the caption "analysis". Cruel, brief, and pinned up in three pubs by Sunday lunchtime.
news.wLoseOn1: The losing run has outlasted the anger. The phone-ins have gone quiet, and that is worse.
news.wLoseOn2: Still no win. The terraces have moved from fury to gallows humour, and the away end knows all the punchlines.
news.wLoseOn3: The slump goes on and the man with the flask in row F has started bringing a book. He has renewed every year since 1987. He will renew again. He would just like a reason.
news.wKid1: Every scout in the league has {clubPoss} {age}-year-old {pos} {player} in their notebook. Coaches say the polish has come on this season. One director of rugby: "That will cost a fortune in a year. Move now or regret it."
news.wKid2: {player}, {age}, is the name scouts keep writing down twice. {club} know exactly what they have. Keeping it quiet is another matter.
news.wKid3: The stopwatch brigade were out in force again for {clubPoss} {pos} {player}. He is {age}. The men in the stand with clipboards were not there for the tea.
news.wMerc1: , and his agent is already dialling
news.wMerc2: , and his agent says it loudest
news.wMerc3: , and this one pays an agent to be loud
news.wGrumble1: Sources say {player} ({pos}, rated among your best) trained away from the main group on Monday. His camp's message: "He didn't come here to hold tackle bags." The mood is souring{merc1_k}.
news.wGrumble2: {player} has started every week the same way: brilliant in training, absent from the team sheet. People around the squad have begun saying "situation" out loud{merc2_k}.
news.wGrumble3: The cameras caught {player} watching the warm-up from the bench again, jaw set. A {pos} of his standing does not stay quiet forever{merc3_k}. The dressing room is watching how you handle it.
news.wDeadlineAhead: Two rounds until the mid-season deadline. Chairmen panic, agents feast, and medicals happen in car parks at midnight. Expect the phone to ring.
news.wWindowShut: Deadline chaos over. Directors of rugby emerge blinking into the daylight to explain themselves. The market is shut until the summer.
news.runDies: {n} competitive games unbeaten, and it ends here. The dressing room is quiet. Every other side in the league will sleep a bit easier tonight.
news.run8Subj: Eight unbeaten: the league has noticed
news.run8: {club} have not lost a competitive game in two months, and opponents have started circling the fixture. Expect every one of them to play their cup final against you.
news.run12Subj: Twelve unbeaten: the target on the shirt is real
news.run12: A dozen without defeat. Opposition coaches are planning their whole week around you, and neutrals are turning up hoping to see the run end.
news.run16: Nobody at the club will say it, so everybody else is saying it for them: invincible. Sixteen competitive matches without defeat.

news.debtDemand: The club is {debt} in the red. The board expects the books to be balanced.
news.debtConcern: The club is {debt} in the red. The board would like to see that number come down.

news.milestoneV2: {what_k} for {player}. The kit man has had a shirt printed and the squad have been rehearsing a speech nobody will admit to writing.
news.milestoneV3: {player} brings up {what_k}. The club photographer is booked for Tuesday, and the dressing room has already decided who pays for the cake.

news.fansUpSubj: The terraces are in full voice
news.fansUp: The songs have new verses and the away allocations are selling out. {stadium} has become a hard place to go.
news.fansDown: Sections of the support turned on the team this week. Banners are being painted and the phone-ins are merciless. Home games will feel colder until the results turn.

news.keptPlans: You told {player} he was in your plans, and the team sheets backed it up. He knocked on your door after training: "You didn't have to promise me anything, and you kept it anyway. Thanks, coach." The rest of the dressing room noticed too.
news.keptMinutes: {player} got the minutes you promised him. He found you in the corridor after the session: "You said I'd get my chance and you kept your word. I won't forget that, coach." The academy coach is pleased too: "That's how you bring one through."
news.keptDeal: {player} has his new deal, as you said he would. The senior pros noticed.
news.brokePlans: You told {player} he was in your plans {n} weeks ago. He has barely seen the pitch since. The conversation has leaked to the squad, and his agent is already briefing that "the manager's word means nothing at this club."
news.brokeMinutes: {player} was promised minutes and got none. He trained with headphones in all week, and the academy coach has stopped defending you in the canteen.
news.brokeDeal: {player} is still waiting for the deal you as good as promised him. He held off other offers on your word and now feels strung along. The older heads in the squad are watching how this ends.

news.rankThree: The rankings have {nationThe_k} at {pos} in the world, the highest of your time in charge. The pundits have started saying it out loud: this side could win the lot.
news.shortlistAlert: The chief scout rings it in: {player} ({pos}, {short}) {alert_k}
news.slListed: has been transfer-listed by {short}. He'll come cheap, and he won't be on the list long.
news.slExpiring: is out of contract this summer and {short} haven't tied him down. He could come on a free.
news.slForm: is in the form of his life ({form}). His price is climbing by the week.
news.armband: The captaincy was vacant and it goes to the most senior player in the squad: {player} ({age}, {pos}){how_k}. Nobody argued.
news.badBlood: There's proper needle between the clubs now: {reason_k}. The next meeting will be spicy. Expect a few cards and a hostile crowd.
news.capEmbargo: A second breach in two seasons. The league fine {club} {fine} and impose a transfer embargo for next season: no signings, in or out of the window, until the wage bill is back inside {cap}/wk. The board is furious. Bring the bill down or the sanction repeats.
news.capFineSubj: Salary cap: the club is fined
news.capFine: {club} finished the season {over}/wk over the {cap}/wk salary cap. The league fine the club {fine} and put it on notice: breach it again next season and the punishment is a transfer embargo. Two players can be named marquee and taken out of the calculation, and academy players never counted.
news.deputationSubj: The senior players ask for a meeting
news.deputation: A group of senior players come into the office and shut the door. Polite, but blunt. {a} and {b} have been left to drift, and they want to know who is in charge. Deal with both in the {room_k} and win on Saturday, and that should be the end of it.
news.deputationNamed: {player} comes into the office and shuts the door. Polite, but blunt: the squad have watched {a} and {b} drift and want to know who's in charge. Sort both out in the {room_k}, win on Saturday, and you won't see this again.
news.deputationNamedV2: {player} knocks and asks for five minutes, which becomes twenty. The squad have seen {a} and {b} left unresolved and want to know whether anyone is going to deal with them. Settle both in the {room_k} and win on Saturday, and the knock won't come again.
news.deputationNamedV3: {player} arrives with the look of someone who drew the short straw. The message: {a} and {b} have been left to drift, and the group have noticed. Answer both in the {room_k}, get a win, and the conversation is over.
news.incidentDrifts: Two weeks on and nothing has been said. The squad have noticed that {player} got away with it.
news.adminMine: {short} couldn't pay what they owed, and the board has filed for administration. The debt is cleared. The price is {n} points docked before a ball is kicked, and two of your biggest earners gone. You start on minus {n}.
news.adminOther: {club} have gone into administration after a season they could not pay for. The league will dock them {n} points, and two senior players have already been released as the administrators cut the wage bill.
news.insolvencyWarningSubj: The board: we cannot go on like this
news.insolvencyWarning: The finance director has put a number in front of the board that nobody can live with: at this rate {short} do not survive the summer. A club that cannot pay goes into administration and starts the next season on minus {n}. Sell somebody, cut the wage bill, or fill the ground.
news.briefSent: {fee} of expenses, a hire car and a brief: {brief_k} {where_k}. {scout} ({badge_k} badge) files his report in {n} weeks. The longer he's out, the more rugby he sees.

postcard.one:
{weeksIn} weeks into the brief. "{verdict_k} I'll keep looking. About {n} week till I write it all up."

He is properly scouted now: a true reading, not a range.
postcard.other:
{weeksIn} weeks into the brief. "{verdict_k} I'll keep looking. About {n} weeks till I write it all up."

He is properly scouted now: a true reading, not a range.

news.postcardKeen: Seen {player} twice now and I'd put my name to him. {age}, {pos_k} {at_k}, and he does the things you can't teach.

scoutMonthly.one:
{weeksIn} weeks on the road. Brief: {brief_k} {where_k}.

New name: {player}, {age}, {pos_k} {at_k}. Names so far: {found}. Report in {n} week.
scoutMonthly.other:
{weeksIn} weeks on the road. Brief: {brief_k} {where_k}.

New name: {player}, {age}, {pos_k} {at_k}. Names so far: {found}. Report in {n} weeks.

scoutMonthlyNone.one:
{weeksIn} weeks on the road. Brief: {brief_k} {where_k}.

No new names this month. Names so far: {found}. Report in {n} week.
scoutMonthlyNone.other:
{weeksIn} weeks on the road. Brief: {brief_k} {where_k}.

No new names this month. Names so far: {found}. Report in {n} weeks.

news.postcardMaybe: {player} is worth a mention. {age}, {pos_k} {at_k}. Not the answer on his own, but I wouldn't rule him out.
news.scoutReport: {months} months, {n} {names_k}, {good} of them he would sign tomorrow. Top of the list: {player}, {age}, {pos_k} {at_k} - {note_k} The full report is in the Transfer Centre, and every name on it is now fully scouted.
news.noteA1: Ready now. He'd walk into your XV.
news.noteA2: Best in his position I've seen all trip.
news.noteA3: Don't let this one get away.
news.noteB1: Improves the squad now, and there's more to come.
news.noteB2: A season of proper coaching and he's a starter.
news.noteC1: Squad depth, nothing more, but honest with it.
news.noteC2: Useful in a crisis. Not one to build around.
news.noteC3: Worth a look if the price is right.
news.noteD1: Had one good game while I was there. Not convinced.
news.noteD2: I've seen better, but someone will pay for him.
news.wcDrawSubj: World Championship draw: the rankings pick the pools
news.wcDrawWSubj: World Championship draw: the rankings pick the pools
news.wcDraw:
The World Championship pools are set, seeded from the world rankings. Top seeds: {top_l}.
Four pools, five nations each, and somewhere in there a group of death.
news.wcDrawSeededSubj: World Championship draw: the rankings pick the pools
news.wcDrawSeeded:
The World Championship pools are set, seeded from the world rankings. Top seeds: {top_l}.
{nationCap_k} go in as the {seed_o} seed - anything short of {bar_k}.
news.wcBarSemi: the semi-finals will be a failure
news.wcBarKnockout: the knockouts would still be par
news.sponsorSigned: {sponsor} take the {slot_k} for {yrs_k} at {weekly} a week. The commercial department is pleased with itself, and the money starts arriving on Friday.{naming_k}
news.sponsorSignedClause: {sponsor} take the {slot_k} for {yrs_k} at {weekly} a week, with a clause: {clause_k} Meet it and the club have done very well out of this.{naming_k}
news.sponsorSignedPerf: {sponsor} take the {slot_k} for {yrs_k} at {weekly} a week guaranteed, with bonuses worth up to {top} a season on results. The league target is position {target} or better.{naming_k}
news.sponsorNaming: The signage vans arrive Monday: the ground plays as {stadium} for the length of the deal.
news.sponsorExpires: The {slot_k} is out of contract: {sponsor} have reached the end of their term. The commercial department has rolled on with {newSponsor} at {rate} a week. That's under the going rate, because nobody was there to argue for more. Better offers are on the table if you want them.
news.sponsorBonus: The season's performance bonuses are in: {met} of {n} targets met across the club's sponsorship deals, worth {amount}. Paid by {sponsors}.
news.sponsorBonusNone: Not one of the {n} performance targets in the club's sponsorship deals was met this season, so the bonuses pay nothing. The guaranteed fees still stand.
news.aCoachNamed: {coach} has filed the A League report.
news.aCoachNamedV2: The A League notes are in from {coach}.
news.aCoachNamedV3: {coach} reports from the A League weekend.
news.aCoachAnon: The academy coach has filed the A League report.
news.aCoachAnonV2: The A League notes are in from the academy.
news.aCoachAnonV3: The academy staff report from the A League weekend.
news.aWonLine0: Results aren't the point at this level. Nobody's handing the win back, though.
news.aWonLine1: He was happier with the last twenty minutes than with the scoreline.
news.aWonLine2: A win, and more importantly nobody came off holding anything.
news.aWonLine3: The coach says the front row grew up a fortnight in eighty minutes.
news.aWonLine4: Two of them will train with the seniors this week off the back of that.
news.aWonLine5: He signed off with one line: "That is the standard now."
news.aLostLine0: Nobody's fussed about the score. The minutes were the point, and the young lads got plenty.
news.aLostLine1: A heavy beating. The coach shrugged it off: this is what the A League is for.
news.aLostLine2: He wants you to know which three kept going at 20 down, because those are the three who will make it.
news.aLostLine3: Chastening, and useful. The video session will be quiet and long.
news.aLostLine4: "Nobody hid." That was his whole report.
news.aLostLine5: The coach reckons they were beaten by bigger men, and that bigger men are a matter of time.
news.memoNoRugby: Form: no competitive rugby in this window. International break, nothing to judge.
news.memoTable: League: {pos_o} in the table on the season so far.
news.memoMoney: Finances: {word_k} at {bal}, transfer budget {budget}. Wage bill {bill}/wk.
news.memoMoneyCap: Finances: {word_k} at {bal}, transfer budget {budget}. Wage bill {bill}/wk against a {cap} cap, {room} of room.
news.memoMoneyOver: Finances: {word_k} at {bal}, transfer budget {budget}. Wage bill {bill}/wk against a {cap} cap - WE ARE OVER IT.
news.memoVA0: Verdict: the boardroom is delighted. Keep going and this becomes your club.
news.memoVA1: Verdict: nobody here wants to talk about anything except how well this is going.
news.memoVA2: Verdict: you have the board's full backing, and you have earned it.
news.memoVB0: Verdict: the board is satisfied. Nothing here that a good month would not improve.
news.memoVB1: Verdict: broadly happy. We would like to see this kicked on rather than held.
news.memoVB2: Verdict: solid. The directors are comfortable and would like to stay that way.
news.memoVC0: Verdict: we're patient, but not endlessly. We expect results to turn.
news.memoVC1: Verdict: the mood upstairs is wait and see. Give us something to point at.
news.memoVC2: Verdict: neither pleased nor panicking. The next month matters more than this one.
news.memoVD0: Verdict: concern, stated plainly. This has to improve and soon.
news.memoVD1: Verdict: the board is worried, and some of it is being said out loud.
news.memoVD2: Verdict: we are not where anybody expected to be. We need a response.
news.memoVE0: Verdict: this is a formal warning. The board is discussing your position.
news.memoVE1: Verdict: the directors have lost patience. Results now, or a decision gets made for you.
news.memoVE2: Verdict: your position is under review. There is no gentler way to put it.
news.notOut: You turned {age} this summer, which in this trade is when the press start asking the question. No hurry. You can retire whenever you like from here, and at {forced} the decision gets made for you.
news.aTitleMine: The A side finish top of the {comp}: {w} wins from {p}, {pf} points scored. Nobody hangs a flag for it. The coaches know what it means, though: some of these lads will be in your matchday 23 within three years.
