styles.atk_directDesc: Straight at them: one-out carriers off the ruck, pick-and-go and few passes to drop. Wins the gain line and the penalties that come with it and loses few balls, but makes fewer clean breaks.
styles.atk_podsDesc: A forward on each edge, a pod of three either side of the middle and the backs behind them as the second option. Balanced and hard to read, and the pod shapes among your moves fit it best.
styles.atk_widthDesc: Flat passes to a screen of runners, with the ball swept round the back of them to the outside channels. More line breaks, but a long pass can be picked off and the ruck is left light.
styles.atk_kickDesc: Box kicks and contestable kicks with a chase line under them: territory, the aerial battle and pressure on their back three. Fewer phases and fewer line breaks, and more kicks that can be charged down.
styles.atk_offloadDesc: Keep the ball alive in the tackle and play what is in front of you. The most line breaks of any style, and the most turnovers. It costs legs.
styles.def_driftDesc: Up, then out: the line slides across one man and pushes play towards the touchline, which never misses a tackle. Gives away few penalties.
styles.def_blitzTag: Line speed, no time on the ball
styles.def_blitzDesc: The whole line comes up fast and together, into the carrier before the attack can build speed. Wins the ball behind the gain line, but the offside calls add up, the space in behind is empty and it costs legs.
styles.def_pendulumDesc: A standard line, with the back three swinging behind it to cover the kick space: the ball-side wing up, the full-back deep, the far wing in the middle. Safe, but the line in front is a man short.
styles.def_manDesc: Every defender takes one attacker and stays with that runner. Simple to drill, and how it goes depends on who wins the one-on-ones.
styles.def_chokeTag: Hold them up, win the ball
styles.def_chokeDesc: Tackle high, keep the carrier on their feet and force the maul or the held-up ball. Wins the ball back more than any other defence, but it is narrow, and a side that moves it wide finds the edges thin.
styles.cAtk_direct1: {team} keep coming straight at {opp}, and {def_k} cannot hold the gain line.
styles.cAtk_direct2: Carry after carry from {team}, and every one of them over the gain line.
styles.cAtk_pods1: The pods from {team} ask questions right across the field, and {def_k} has no answer.
styles.cAtk_pods2: One pod after another goes forward, and {team} have {opp} on the back foot.
styles.cAtk_width1: {team} go wide at every chance, and {def_k} cannot get out to the edges.
styles.cAtk_width2: A flat pass, a screen, the sweep round the back: {team} are stretching {opp} to the touchline.
styles.cAtk_kick1: Up and under from {team}, and the chase is on {opp} before the ball comes down. There is nobody behind {def_k}.
styles.cAtk_kick2: {team} kick in behind the rushing line again, and {opp} have to turn and chase.
styles.cAtk_offload1: The ball comes out of the tackle again and {team} are through. {opp} are scrambling.
styles.cAtk_offload2: {team} keep the ball alive in contact, and the offloads are pulling {def_k} apart.
styles.cDef_drift1: {team} slide across and push {opp} towards the touchline, and {atk_k} runs out of room.
styles.cDef_drift2: The drift is on, and {team} shepherd {opp} into touch.
styles.cDef_blitz1: The blitz from {team} catches {opp} behind the gain line.
styles.cDef_blitz2: {team} fly up off the line and give {opp} no time on the ball.
styles.cDef_pendulum1: The back three are exactly where the kick comes down: {team} have read {atk_k}.
styles.cDef_pendulum2: {opp} kick, and the cover from {team} is already waiting for it.
styles.cDef_man1: Every runner from {opp} has a defender square in front. Man-to-man, and nobody gets free.
styles.cDef_man2: {team} have picked up every runner, and {atk_k} has nowhere to go.
styles.cDef_choke1: Held up! The choke tackle from {team} stops {opp} dead, and the carry goes nowhere.
styles.cDef_choke2: {team} tackle high and hold the ball up, and {atk_k} is playing straight into their hands.
styles.cTurn_drift: {player} reads the pass out wide, and {team} have the turnover.
styles.cTurn_blitz: {player} is up in a flash, and {team} win the ball back.
styles.cTurn_pendulum: {player} sweeps up the loose ball in the cover, and the ball belongs to {team}.
styles.cTurn_man: {player} wins the one-on-one and rips the ball away. Turnover to {team}.
styles.cTurn_choke: Choke tackle! {player} holds the carrier up and {team} win the turnover.
styles.movesElsewhere: Set moves are chosen in the Playbook.
styles.tuneNote: Playing {atk} with the ball and {def} without it. The dials below fine-tune it.
styles.fitPoor: Your XV does not suit it
styles.movesKick: Fewer phases: the open-play moves suit it less.
styles.oppStyles: Their styles: {atk} in attack, {def} in defence.
styles.edgeAtk_good: Your {mine} attack into their {theirs} defence: the matchup favours you.
styles.edgeAtk_bad: Your {mine} attack into their {theirs} defence: the matchup favours them.
styles.edgeAtk_even: Your {mine} attack into their {theirs} defence: an even matchup.
styles.edgeDef_good: Their {theirs} attack into your {mine} defence: the matchup favours you.
styles.edgeDef_bad: Their {theirs} attack into your {mine} defence: the matchup favours them.
styles.edgeDef_even: Their {theirs} attack into your {mine} defence: an even matchup.
styles.pod_1331Desc: A forward on each edge and two pods of three in the middle: the balanced pod game.
styles.pod_242Desc: Two forwards on each edge and four in the middle: the ball goes wider sooner, with more breaks out wide and a little less go-forward.
styles.pod_nineDesc: One-out runners round the scrum-half: quick ball off short carries, the most gain line and the fewest errors, but fewer breaks.

tt.reactionsSub: every player hears it their own way
tt.pre_calm1: Quiet voice, slow words. You walk the room through the first twenty minutes.
tt.pre_calm2: No theatre. The plan on one whiteboard line, and the pen capped.
tt.pre_faith1: You go round the room and tell each player why the shirt is theirs.
tt.pre_faith2: "I picked this side because I trust it. Go and show them why."
tt.pre_expect1: Standards. Do the basics right for eighty minutes. You don't ask for anything fancier.
tt.pre_expect2: "Win, and win properly." Nothing else needs saying.
tt.pre_fire1: They go out of that door like it owes them money.
tt.pre_fire2: Two sentences, both loud. The front row are first out of the door.
tt.pre_silent1: Nothing from you again, and the room noticed. Your assistant says so quietly on the way out.
tt.pre_silent2: Another silent dressing room. Your assistant catches your eye: the group was waiting for a word.
tt.ht_calm1: Calm and matter-of-fact. Two fixes on the whiteboard, nothing more.
tt.ht_calm2: You bring the temperature down. Stick to the plan, make the tackle in front of you.
tt.ht_faith1: "Forty minutes. I know what this group has in it." You mean every word.
tt.ht_faith2: You tell them the game is still there to be won, and that you trust them to win it.
tt.ht_praise1: You name three things they did exactly right and ask for more of the same.
tt.ht_praise2: You are delighted with that half, and you tell them so.
tt.ht_demand1: More, you ask. Not different, just more.
tt.ht_demand2: "That was fine. Fine does not win this." You want a better forty.
tt.ht_criticise1: You go through the half one mistake at a time and spare nobody.
tt.ht_criticise2: Out comes the hairdryer. Every error is named, out loud.
tt.ht_fire1: A cup of tea goes flying. Forty minutes of everything, you tell them.
tt.ht_fire2: Voice up, collar loose. The room goes silent, then very loud.
tt.verdict_good: It lands: most of the room looks ready.
tt.verdict_mixed: It lands with some and not with others.
tt.verdict_bad: It misses: the room was in no mood for that.
